Grybow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Siołkowa, Poland

Not demolished. Grybów, founded under Magdeburg Law in 1340, saw Jewish settlement from the mid-18th century, with an independent community established before 1870; 1919 brought antisemitic riots led by local peasants and youth. Germans relocated Jews from surrounding towns to Grybów early in the occupation; a ghetto formed at the end of 1941 was liquidated on August 20, 1942, with about 360 people shot at Biała Niżna and roughly 150 elderly and sick residents (many brought from Nowy Sącz) executed directly at this cemetery. This cemetery, established in the second half of the 18th century, includes a small WWI military section originally holding 7 graves (4 marked tombstones survive); German soldiers desecrated the site during WWII, using its stones to pave a local brewery's courtyard. A 2019 memorial project, 'People, Not Numbers,' inscribed the names of 1,774 people imprisoned and murdered from the Grybów Ghetto onto a dedicated 'Matzevah of Remembrance.'
